mainTopic: Several explanations of the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about proving ownership with a document: אותיות, unfit or missing witnesses, קיום of an admitted שטר, and לברר.
overview: This amud keeps trying to explain a ברייתא where רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about proving ownership of land. רב דימי says they argue about whether the rights in a document (אותיות) pass by handing it over. אביי objects that this would make רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradict himself. אביי then says the argument is about a document with an unfit witness, and ties it to the dispute between רבי אלעזר (handing-over witnesses count) and רבי מאיר (signing witnesses count). רבי אבא's teaching knocks this down, so רבי אבינא moves the case to a שטר with no witnesses signed on it at all. The גמרא then offers another explanation: they argue about whether a מודה בשטר שכתבו still needs קיום. A second ברייתא seems to show their views the other way around. The גמרא answers either by flipping the names, or by saying the first argument is about לברר, whether a person must back up every claim he makes. A story with רבי אבא and רבי יצחק נפחא illustrates לברר, and רבי אבא's final objection from רב גידל continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can the rights in a document be acquired by handing it over?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains the dispute: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that אותיות are not acquired through מסירה, while רבי holds that they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the letters of a document are not acquired by handing it over. רבי holds that they are acquired by handing it over.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of רב דימי's explanation of a dispute between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי. He says the whole dispute depends on whether handing over a document transfers the rights written in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב דימי's case, land was sold, and the buyer then passed the bill of sale on to a third person. According to רבי, that handover is a valid transfer, so the document alone proves ownership. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the handover does not work, so the third person has to rely on a חזקה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Letters: the rights written in a document
Are acquired
Handing over the document itself
Holds, is of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: 'Letters' here does not mean the alphabet. It means the legal claim or rights recorded in the document.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
letters are not acquired by handing over [the document],
phrases.notes: 'Letters' means the rights written in the document, such as a claim to land.

phrases.english: and Rabbi holds:
letters are acquired by handing over [the document].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues רב דימי's explanation of the ברייתא from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: אותיות are not acquired through מסירה. רבי: they are.

steps.title: אביי: this contradicts רבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that saying רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds אותיות are not acquired through מסירה disagrees with what רבה said.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, you are disagreeing with the Master.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב דימי. He points out that his explanation goes against an earlier statement of רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבה had explained that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that אותיות are acquired through מסירה. רב דימי has just said the opposite. אביי is pointing out this clash.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
A disagreement
The Master: a title of respect, here referring to רבה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so, this is a disagreement with the Master!
phrases.notes: 'The Master' is רבה, אביי's teacher, who explained רבן שמעון בן גמליאל the opposite way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִם כֵּן, פְּלוּגְתָּא לִדְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the explanation given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds אותיות are not acquired through מסירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה already stated that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the opposite, so the two explanations clash.

steps.title: רב דימי: so let it disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that he is free to disagree with רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: So let it disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brushes off אביי's objection. He says he does not have to agree with רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two אמוראים are allowed to disagree about how to explain a תנא. So pointing out a conflict with רבה is not, on its own, a real problem. This answer pushes אביי to explain why his objection is serious.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it disagree

phrases.english: He said to him: So let it disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers אביי's objection in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the disagreement with another אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A conflict with רבה would disprove רב דימי's explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב דימי is free to explain רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differently from רבה.

steps.title: אביי's real point: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the earlier ברייתא can only be read the way רבה read it, so רב דימי's version would make רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradict himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I am telling you. The ברייתא can only be explained the way the Master explained it. If so, there is a difficulty: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradicts רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי clarifies and strengthens his objection. The problem is not just disagreeing with רבה, but an internal contradiction in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier ברייתא, the only workable reading is רבה's, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds אותיות are acquired through מסירה. If here he holds they are not, then the same תנא says two opposite things. That is a real קשיא, and 'let it disagree' cannot answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I am saying to you
A ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the תנאים)
Can be explained
A difficulty

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule of the גמרא: an אמורא may disagree with another אמורא, but his explanation must not make a single תנא contradict himself.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying to you:
The ברייתא cannot be explained
phrases.notes: This is the earlier ברייתא that רבה explained, not the one being discussed now.

phrases.english: except the way the Master explained it,
and if so, there is a difficulty

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל!
phrases.english: of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This rejects רב דימי's answer in step 3 by sharpening the objection from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's explanation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier ברייתא forces רבה's reading, so רב דימי's reading creates a self-contradiction in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's views.

steps.title: אביי's new explanation: one of the witnesses was unfit
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the case differently: one of the witnesses on the document turned out to be a relative or otherwise disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: What are we dealing with here? A case where one of them was found to be a relative or disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops רב דימי's explanation and gives his own. The case involves a document with a witness who turned out to be unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the dispute no longer depends on whether אותיות are acquired through מסירה, so the contradiction disappears. Instead, the case is about a document that has a problem, because one of its witnesses is a קרוב or a פסול. The next step shows how this explains the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces a new approach
What case are we dealing with here?
A relative: disqualified as a witness
Disqualified for another reason

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where one of them was found
phrases.notes: 'One of them' means one of the witnesses who signed the document.

phrases.english: to be a relative or disqualified;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This replaces רב דימי's explanation from step 1, which was knocked down in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute depends on whether אותיות are acquired through מסירה, which makes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case involves a document with an unfit witness, so the contradiction does not come up.

steps.title: אביי links the dispute to רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his explanation. רבי follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that the handing-over witnesses make a document work. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל follows רבי מאיר, who holds that the signing witnesses make it work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they are arguing about the same thing that רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר argue about. רבי holds like רבי אלעזר, who says that the witnesses who watch the document being handed over are what make it work. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds like רבי מאיר, who says that the witnesses who sign the document are what make it work.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is completing the answer he started in step 5. He explains why a document with one disqualified witness would be treated differently by רבי and by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, אביי said one of the signed witnesses turned out to be a relative or otherwise disqualified. Now he gives the reason for the disagreement. If the handing-over witnesses are what count (רבי אלעזר), a bad signature does not matter, so רבי accepts the שטר. If the signing witnesses are what count (רבי מאיר), a bad signature ruins it, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who see the document being handed over
Witnesses who sign the document
Literally 'cut'; here it means they make the document take effect
A dispute or disagreement

steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר is the background for the rest of this section. Every move that follows argues about how to apply it.

phrases.english: And in the dispute of רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר
they are disagreeing:
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: רבי holds like רבי אלעזר,
who says: the witnesses of the handing-over make it effective,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds like רבי מאיר,
who says: the signing witnesses make it effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer from step 5 by giving the underlying reason for the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the dispute in the ברייתא to an earlier, known dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seemed to contradict himself about אותיות and מסירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is not about אותיות at all. It is about whether signing witnesses or handing-over witnesses make a שטר work.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי אבא: רבי אלעזר also rejects a flawed document
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא taught that even רבי אלעזר agrees a document with a built-in flaw is invalid. So רבי cannot accept a document with a disqualified witness by following רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אבא say: רבי אלעזר agreed that a document that is flawed from within itself is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's explanation. It quotes רבי אבא, who said that רבי אלעזר himself would not accept a document with a flaw built into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's case is a document signed by a disqualified witness. That is exactly a document 'flawed from within.' רבי אלעזר only says handing-over witnesses are enough when nothing bad is written on the document. So רבי, following רבי אלעזר, could not accept אביי's document either.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that is flawed from within itself, such as one signed by unfit witnesses
Invalid
Agrees or concedes

phrases.english: But didn't רבי אבא say:
רבי אלעזר agreed
about a document flawed from within, that it is invalid!
phrases.notes: He means the flaw is right on the paper itself, like unfit witnesses signed on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's case from steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי, following רבי אלעזר, accepts a document with a disqualified signed witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר admits that a document with unfit witnesses signed on it is invalid. So רבי אלעזר's view cannot be the reason to accept it.

steps.title: רבי אבינא: the dispute is about a שטר with no witnesses at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבינא adjusts אביי's explanation. Everyone agrees that a document whose signed witnesses were found false is invalid. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only argue about a שטר with no signed witnesses at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבינא said: Everyone agrees that if it is written on the document, 'We looked into the testimony of the witnesses, and their testimony was found to be false,' it is invalid, as רבי אבא said. They argue only about a document that has no witnesses on it at all. רבי holds like רבי אלעזר, who says the handing-over witnesses make it work. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds like רבי מאיר, who says the signing witnesses make it work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבינא gives a new version of אביי's answer so that it avoids רבי אבא's challenge. He changes the case from a document with a bad witness to a document with no witnesses signed on it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document with false or unfit signed witnesses is flawed from within, so everyone rejects it, even רבי אלעזר. A blank document with no signatures has no flaw written on it. That is where רבי אלעזר says handing-over witnesses are enough. So רבי accepts that שטר, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, following רבי מאיר, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We looked into'; the court checked the witnesses
Testimony found to be false
A document with no witnesses signed on it at all
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי אבינא's version, everyone rejects a document whose signed witnesses are false. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue only about a שטר with no signatures, following the dispute between רבי אלעזר (handing-over witnesses count) and רבי מאיר (signing witnesses count). Step 9 offers a different explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not keep picturing אביי's case of a disqualified witness. רבי אבינא has switched the case to a שטר with no witnesses signed on it at all.

phrases.english: Rather, רבי אבינא said:
Everyone agrees that if it is written on it:
'We looked into the testimony of the witnesses,'
phrases.notes: This is the court writing on the document that it checked the signatures.

phrases.english: 'and their testimony was found to be false' –
that it is invalid, as רבי אבא said;
they argued only
about a document that has no witnesses on it at all,
for רבי holds like רבי אלעזר,
who says: the witnesses of the handing-over make it effective.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds like רבי מאיר,
who says: the signing witnesses make it effective.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge from step 7 by redefining the case in אביי's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (אוקימתא) to a document with no signed witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about a document with a disqualified signed witness, which even רבי אלעזר would reject.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a document with no signed witnesses. There, the dispute between רבי אלעזר and רבי מאיר applies directly.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A document with false signed witnesses is invalid for everyone. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue only about an unsigned שטר.

steps.title: A new explanation: they argue about a document the signer admits he wrote
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to explain the argument. רבי holds that a מודה בשטר שכתבו does not need קיום, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: they argue about a person who admits he wrote a document, and whether it still needs to be proven in court. רבי holds that if he admits he wrote it, there is no need to prove it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that it still needs to be proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate way to explain what רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל are arguing about. This time it has nothing to do with false or missing witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is about a case where the other side admits he wrote the document but still disputes it. According to רבי, his admission is enough, so the document can be used without proving the signatures. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the document must still be proven in בית דין before anyone can rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: the גמרא is introducing a different answer
A person who admits that he wrote the document
To prove it in court: confirming that the signatures are real (קיום שטר)
They are arguing about

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the whole argument onto a well-known question in the laws of documents: does an admission take the place of proving the signatures?

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
about one who admits a document that he wrote
whether it needs to be ratified, they disagree,
phrases.notes: 'Ratify' means proving in בית דין that the witnesses' signatures are real.

phrases.english: for רבי holds:
one who admits a document that he wrote,
it does not need to be ratified.
And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds:
it needs to be ratified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּמוֹדֶה בַּשְּׁטָר שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַיְּימוֹ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the argument instead of רבי אבינא's explanation about a שטר with no signed witnesses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the subject of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about which witnesses make a שטר work, or about a שטר without signed witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about whether a document the signer admits he wrote still needs קיום. רבי says no, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says yes.

steps.title: But a ברייתא shows their opinions the other way around
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new explanation. In a ברייתא about a lender and a borrower grabbing a loan document, רבי requires proving the signatures even though the borrower admits the loan. That looks like the opposite of what was just said in his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard the opposite from them! As a ברייתא teaches: two people are holding on to a document. The lender says, 'It is mine, it fell from me, and you found it.' The borrower says, 'It is yours, but I paid you back.' The document must be proven through its signers. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation by quoting a ברייתא where רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seem to hold the reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the borrower admits he wrote the loan document ('it is yours'), yet רבי still says it must be proven through its signers. That means רבי holds a document that is admitted still needs קיום, which is the opposite of step 9. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says to split the money, which suggests he relies on the admission without קיום.

keyTerms.meaning: We heard the opposite from them
Grasping, both holding on tightly
Lender / borrower
The document must be proven through its signing witnesses
They divide it between them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the borrower in the ברייתא denies the loan. He agrees it was a real loan ('it is yours') and only claims he paid it back. That admission is exactly why the case is about מודה בשטר שכתבו.

phrases.english: But we heard the opposite from them!
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Two people are grasping a document,
the lender says, "It is mine
and it fell from me and you found it,"
phrases.notes: He means the borrower found the note after the lender dropped it.

phrases.english: and the borrower says, "It is yours
and I paid it back to you":
the document must be ratified through its signers.
These are the words of רבי.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יַחְלוֹקוּ.
phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: they divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new explanation from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי holds a מודה בשטר שכתבו does not need קיום, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that it does.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא the borrower admits writing the note, yet רבי requires proving its signatures. So רבי holds an admitted note does need קיום, which is the reverse of step 9.

steps.title: Recalling an old question: why doesn't רבי say to split it, like the garment case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins retelling an earlier discussion of that ברייתא. It had asked why רבי does not follow the משנה where two people holding a garment each swear and split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this ברייתא before and asked: doesn't רבי agree with what we learned in a משנה? Two people are holding a garment. This one says, 'I found it,' and that one says, 'I found it.' This one swears he owns no less than half of it, that one swears he owns no less than half of it, and they split it. So why doesn't רבי say to split the loan document too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is recalling an older discussion of the ברייתא it just quoted. This sets up the next move, which will clarify what רבי really holds about an admitted document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה of the garment teaches that when two people both hold an item and both claim it, they split it. The lender and borrower are also both holding the note, so we would expect רבי to say 'split it' as well. רבי's refusal to do so needs an explanation, and that explanation will show how he views a document that the signer admits he wrote.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it: the גמרא is recalling an earlier discussion
Does he not hold
Two people holding a garment, the famous first משנה of בבא מציעא
He must swear an oath

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
and does רבי not hold that which we learned in a משנה:
Two people are holding a garment,
phrases.notes: This is the very first משנה of בבא מציעא.

phrases.english: this one says, "I found it,"
and that one says, "I found it":

phrases.aramaic: זֶה יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵחֶצְיָהּ,
phrases.english: this one swears that he owns no less than half of it,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵחֶצְיָהּ,
phrases.english: and that one swears that he owns no less than half of it,
and they divide it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ – וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Recalls an earlier discussion of the ברייתא quoted in step 10, preparing to show how that ברייתא reveals רבי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling in the ברייתא that the note must be proven through its signers instead of being split.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that two people holding an item each swear and split it. The lender and borrower are both holding the note, so רבי should also rule that they split it.

steps.title: רבא explains that the argument is only about an unproven document
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב נחמן says that everyone agrees a proven שטר is split. The argument is only about an unproven one. רבי says a מודה בשטר שכתבו still needs קיום, so without proof the paper is worthless. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says no proof is needed, so they split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: when the document has been proven, everyone agrees the two sides split it. They argue about a document that has not been proven. רבי holds that even if the borrower admits he wrote the שטר, the lender must prove the signatures. If he proves it, he collects half. If not, the document is just a worthless shard. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that if the borrower admits he wrote it, no proof is needed, so they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer that was given in the earlier discussion to the question from step 11, 'Why doesn't רבי follow the משנה of two people holding a garment?' The answer: רבי does follow it, but only once the document is proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא shows that רבי agrees with the 'split it' rule of the garment משנה, but only for a proven document. The real argument is whether the borrower's admission is enough to make the document usable. That leaves רבי saying 'proof is needed' and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying 'no proof is needed.' This is exactly the reverse of what step 9 said in their names, which is the contradiction raised in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: A document whose witnesses' signatures were proven in בית דין
A borrower who admits that he wrote the loan document
To prove the document by confirming the signatures
They split it (each side gets half)
Just a shard: a worthless piece of paper

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ברייתות. Here רבי is the one who requires proof. In step 9 רבי was the one who did NOT require proof. That flip is the whole problem the גמרא is about to solve.

phrases.english: And Rava said that Rav Naḥman said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּמְקוּיָּים – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּיַחֲלוֹקוּ.
phrases.english: With a proven document, everyone agrees that they split it.
phrases.notes: This is the garment משנה's rule from step 11: two people holding something split it.

phrases.english: Where they argue is a document that is not proven.
Rabbi holds: one who admits that he wrote a document,
the lender still needs to prove it.
And if he proves it, he collects half,
and if not, it is just a shard.
And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה בִּשְׁטָר שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ – אֵין צָרִיךְ לְקַיְּימוֹ,
phrases.english: one who admits that he wrote a document, the lender does not need to prove it,
and so they split it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בִּמְקוּיָּים דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question retold in step 11. The answer also spells out why step 10 sees a contradiction with step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the argument: limits it to an unproven document
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי seems to ignore the garment משנה's rule of splitting.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי splits a proven document. He only argues about an unproven one, because he requires קיום even when the borrower admits writing it.

steps.title: Flip the names in one of the ברייתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction with one word: reverse the opinions of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in one of the ברייתות so that both match.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between step 9 and step 12 by switching the names in one ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each Sage now holds one consistent view about whether a מודה בשטר שכתבו needs קיום. The contradiction came from a mix-up in which name went with which opinion, not from a real change of mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it: switch which Sage said which opinion

phrases.english: Reverse it.
phrases.notes: He means: switch the names of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in one of the two ברייתות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between the view in step 9 and the view laid out in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל each contradict themselves between the two ברייתות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Swap the names in one ברייתא, and each Sage is consistent.

steps.title: Keep the names, but the first argument is about לברר
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: don't flip anything. The first ברייתא is not about קיום at all. It is about לברר, whether a person must back up every claim he makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: actually, don't reverse it. Rather, here they argue about verifying (לברר).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer that keeps the names as they are. It is setting up an explanation of what 'לברר' means, which continues right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first ברייתא is about whether a person must prove every claim he makes, then it says nothing about whether a מודה בשטר שכתבו needs קיום. Then the two ברייתות never clash, and no names need to be switched.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another answer
Actually, don't reverse the opinions
To verify: having to prove every claim one makes
They argue

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא method. Instead of changing the text, the גמרא changes what the argument is about, and the contradiction disappears.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Actually, don't reverse it,
rather, here they argue about verifying.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the first ברייתא from step 9. The explanation of 'verifying' continues right after this line.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ, אֶלָּא הָכָא בִּלְבָרֵר קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second way to settle the same contradiction that step 13 settled by flipping the names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the argument (a different issue, not קיום)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first ברייתא is about whether a מודה בשטר שכתבו needs קיום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא is about לברר, so it does not clash with the second ברייתא.

steps.title: The case of רבי אבא and the named witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a real story to show what לברר means. A borrower says he repaid in front of two named people, and the judge tells him to bring them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case where רבי אבא owed money to רב יצחק בר יוסף. They came before רבי יצחק נפחא. רבי אבא said: I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so. רבי יצחק said: Let those people come and testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case to show the idea of לברר from Step 14. A borrower names the people who saw him repay, and the judge asks him to bring them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a borrower is believed when he says 'I paid.' Here, though, the borrower added a detail: he named witnesses. The judge wants him to back up that detail, which is exactly the question of לברר.

keyTerms.meaning: Was owed money by him
I repaid you
So-and-so and so-and-so (two specific people he names)
They will testify

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Like this case of Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ זוּזֵי בְּרַבִּי אַבָּא.
phrases.english: who was owed money by Rabbi Abba.
The case came before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha.
He said: I repaid you
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי אבא, the borrower.

phrases.english: in front of so-and-so and so-and-so.
Rabbi Yitzchak said to him:
Let so-and-so and so-and-so come and testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ זוּזֵי בְּרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case of the לברר idea introduced in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of לברר: whether a person must back up a detail he chose to claim.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An actual court case before רבי יצחק נפחא.

steps.title: The borrower objects: repayment does not need witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא protests that he should be believed even if the witnesses don't come, since a loan given with witnesses can be repaid without witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If they don't come, am I not believed? Don't we hold that someone who lends with witnesses does not need to be repaid with witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges the judge's demand. He quotes a known rule that a borrower does not need witnesses to repay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a borrower who says 'I paid' is believed, even without witnesses. So why should his naming witnesses make things worse for him? He is arguing that his main claim is strong enough on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: I am believed
We hold as an established rule
One who lends to another in front of witnesses

phrases.english: He said to him: If they do not come,
am I not believed?!
But don't we hold:
one who lends to his fellow in front of witnesses
does not need to be repaid in front of witnesses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא אָתוּ לָא מְהֵימְנִינָא וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the judge's demand from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's demand that the named witnesses come.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A borrower is believed to say he repaid without witnesses, so the witnesses should not be needed.

steps.title: The judge answers: I follow your own teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that he is following רבי אבא's own report in the name of רב: if you say you paid in front of specific people, those people must come and testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In this matter I hold like the teaching of the master (you). For רבי אבא said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה in the name of רב: Someone who says to his fellow 'I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so' must have them come and testify.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק defends his ruling. He quotes a teaching of רב that רבי אבא himself passed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule (no witnesses needed to repay) is true. But once a borrower names specific witnesses, רב says he must bring them. That means he must back up the claim he chose to make, which is the לברר position.

keyTerms.meaning: The teaching of the master (said politely to the person in front of you)
I hold, I am of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The two רבי יצחק names are different people. רב יצחק בר יוסף is the lender. רבי יצחק נפחא is the judge.

phrases.english: He said to him: In that matter, I
phrases.notes: The speaker is now רבי יצחק נפחא, the judge.

phrases.english: hold like the teaching of the master,
phrases.notes: "The master" means רבי אבא himself, the borrower he is talking to.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Abba said that Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
One who says to his fellow:
"I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so"
needs so-and-so and so-and-so to come and testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא בְּהָהִיא כִּשְׁמַעְתָּא דְמָר סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the borrower's objection in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the general rule: naming specific witnesses creates a claim that must be backed up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A borrower never needs witnesses to show he repaid.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the borrower himself names witnesses, רב says they must come and testify.

steps.title: The borrower pushes back with רב גידל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא counters with another report in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and even רבי did not... The text breaks off here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But רב גידל said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and even רבי did not...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges the judge again. He quotes a ruling from רב that seems to say a person does not need to back up every claim. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the dispute is about לברר. In that dispute, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one who does not require a person to prove every detail he claims, as long as his main claim is strong enough. If the הלכה follows him, then naming witnesses should not force the borrower to bring them. This clashes with the teaching of רב that the judge just quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows the words of
And even רבי did not (sentence continues)

phrases.aramaic: [אֲמַר לֵיהּ,] וְהָא אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't Rav Giddel say that Rav said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets, 'He said to him,' and some don't. Either way, רבי אבא is speaking again.

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: the halacha follows the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and even Rabbi did not

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching of רב (via רבי אבא) that named witnesses must come and testify.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another report from רב rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who does not require a person to back up every claim. So named witnesses should not be needed.
